interactions.label: A neonate with congenital hypothyroidism is often described as a 'good baby' by

params.question: A neonate with congenital hypothyroidism is often described as a 'good baby' by the parents. Which of the following best explains this description?

answers.text: The baby has adequate thyroid function from maternal T4 that crossed the placenta

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Maternal T4 does cross the placenta and provides partial neonatal protection, but it wanes after birth. The baby's apparent calm is not from adequate thyroid function — the infant is hypothyroid and the placid behaviour is a warning sign.

answers.text: The baby is hypotonic and placid due to thyroid hormone deficiency, mistaken for a calm temperament

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! The 'good baby' is actually showing signs of hypothyroidism — hypotonia and lethargy from thyroid hormone deficiency make the infant appear placid, which can dangerously delay clinical suspicion.

answers.text: Congenital hypothyroidism causes excessive melatonin secretion, promoting prolonged sleep

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Melatonin overproduction is not a feature of hypothyroidism. The excessive sleep and placid demeanour result from generalised hypotonia and reduced metabolic activity caused by thyroid hormone deficiency.

answers.text: Neonatal hypothyroidism is asymptomatic in the first six months, so the baby appears well

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Signs of congenital hypothyroidism are present from birth but are often subtle, not absent. Prolonged jaundice, large fontanelle, macroglossia, and hypotonia are early clues that can be missed if not actively sought.

overallFeedback.feedback: The 'good baby' in congenital hypothyroidism is actually showing hypotonia and lethargy from thyroid hormone deficiency. This deceptive presentation is why newborn thyroid screening (heel-prick TSH at day 3–5) is critical — clinical diagnosis alone misses many cases.

Well done! Recognising the deceptively 'good' baby is crucial — hypotonia and lethargy are early signs of congenital hypothyroidism that parents and clinicians may overlook. This is precisely why universal newborn screening (heel-prick TSH) is essential.

interactions.label: Ambiguous genitalia in a neonate requires urgent evaluation. Which of the follow

params.question: Ambiguous genitalia in a neonate requires urgent evaluation. Which of the following best explains why congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) must be screened for as an emergency?

answers.text: Elevated androgens in CAH directly suppress neonatal cardiac output

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Androgens do not directly suppress cardiac function. The cardiovascular collapse in salt-wasting CAH results from mineralocorticoid deficiency causing severe electrolyte derangement and volume depletion.

answers.text: Untreated CAH causes irreversible virilisation within the first 48 hours of life

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While progressive virilisation occurs in untreated CAH, it develops over weeks to months and is not the acute life-threatening emergency. The critical danger is adrenal crisis from salt-wasting.

answers.text: The salt-wasting form of 21-hydroxylase deficiency can cause fatal hyponatraemia and hyperkalaemia within the first weeks of life

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! Salt-wasting CAH (~75% of classic 21-hydroxylase deficiency) causes adrenal crisis with hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia, dehydration, and cardiovascular collapse — typically in the first 1–3 weeks. Every neonate with ambiguous genitalia needs urgent serum electrolyte monitoring.

answers.text: CAH causes acute cortisol toxicity that damages the neonatal brain within hours

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: CAH causes cortisol deficiency, not excess. The emergency arises from combined deficiency of aldosterone (salt-wasting) and cortisol (vascular instability), leading to adrenal crisis — not cortisol toxicity.

overallFeedback.feedback: The emergency in neonatal CAH is the salt-wasting crisis from aldosterone deficiency. Without mineralocorticoids, the neonate rapidly loses sodium and retains potassium, leading to life-threatening dehydration, hyperkalaemia, and cardiovascular collapse within the first 1–3 weeks of life.
Excellent! Recognising that ambiguous genitalia may signal salt-wasting CAH is life-saving. Serum electrolytes and 17-hydroxyprogesterone should be checked urgently in every such neonate.

interactions.label: A 7-year-old child is referred to your clinic for suspected short stature. Which

params.question: A 7-year-old child is referred to your clinic for suspected short stature. Which of the following describes the correct technique for measuring the child's height?

answers.text: Use a calibrated stadiometer with the child barefoot, heels against the backboard, and head in the Frankfort plane

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! The Frankfort plane (lower orbital margin aligned with the external auditory meatus) ensures a reproducible head position. Barefoot, heels together, knees straight, back against the stadiometer — a single inaccurate measurement can lead to wrong conclusions about growth.

answers.text: Measure the child lying supine on the examination table using a standard tape measure

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Supine length measurement is appropriate only for children under 2 years. For children above 2, standing height on a calibrated stadiometer is the correct method. Supine length is typically 0.7–1 cm more than standing height.

answers.text: Have the child stand in shoes against a wall-mounted tape for consistency across visits

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Shoes add variable height and must always be removed. A wall-mounted tape lacks the precision of a calibrated stadiometer. Inconsistent instruments introduce measurement errors that can invalidate growth velocity calculations.

answers.text: Ask the child to stand on tiptoes against a door frame and mark the maximum height reached

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Standing on tiptoes gives a falsely elevated reading, and door-frame marks are non-standardised and imprecise. Clinical growth assessment requires a calibrated stadiometer for accurate, reproducible measurements across visits.

overallFeedback.feedback: Height must be measured using a calibrated stadiometer with the child barefoot, heels together touching the backboard, knees straight, and head positioned in the Frankfort plane. A single inaccurate measurement can invalidate the entire growth assessment.

Well done! Accurate anthropometry is the foundation of growth assessment — every subsequent step (chart plotting, growth velocity calculation, mid-parental height comparison) depends on a precise and reproducible measurement.
